messages:
pagerduty-bot: INCIDENT triggered in #incidents — P1 — Az20 networking: IPv6 DNS timeouts and stalled TCP handshakes. Pager: @jenny

jenny: I’m on it. Seeing high error rate for lookup_latency.v6 in our observability. Is this localized to az20? :rotating_light:

rafael: Edge logs show lots of DNS UDP retries over v6 and subsequent TCP fallback attempts timing out. Many flows stall during TLS handshake — SYN sent, no SYN-ACK after fragmentation attempts.

taylor: I can repro from lab: when we send 1300B UDP queries over v6 path, fragments get dropped. ICMPv6 PTB never seen back at client. Looks like some midpath device blackholing fragments for DNS over UDP and also affecting TCP when PMTUD triggers.

netops: Running live checks: traceroute6 to core DNS from az20-edge shows MTU change at overlay hop. Also seeing incorrect DF clearing on virtual router. Commands I ran:
```
ip -6 route get 2001:db8::53 from 2001:db8::1
sudo tcpdump -i bond0 'icmp6 && ip6[40] == 2' -w /tmp/icmp6.pcap
```

jenny: Customer impact: regenerate metrics show 8% failure rate on v6 name resolution for customers pinned to az20; most fallback to v4 transparently but internal services that require v6-only fail. Notifying customer-success.

cust-success: Reached out to a subset of affected customers. Two reported API latency spikes and one reported service-to-service auth failures. Sending template update.

eng-oncall-bot: On-call handoff: @jenny handing to @rafael in 10m for next shift.

rafael: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Force IPv4 preference for public DNS resolvers via outbound policy (quick) 2) Apply MSS/TCPMSS clamp on edge NATs 3) Temporarily reduce MTU on overlay interfaces to 1500 to avoid fragmentation.

taylor: I prefer option 2+3. MSS clamp avoids TCP stalls quickly; dropping MTU prevents UDP fragmentation. I'll prepare commands.

netops: Note — we saw an automated vendor config change last night enabling "auto-jumbo" on the virtual switch fabric for az20. That likely caused hosts to advertise 9000 while tunnels still assume 1500. Filing SR with vendor.

infra-bot: executing canary change: config/az20/mtu-downsize -> applying to canary-edge-01 (canary=1)

jenny: Apply MSS clamp on canary and measure DNS success rate. If stable for 5m, roll.

rafael: MSS clamp command used on Linux bridges:
```
iptables -t mangle -A POSTROUTING -p tcp -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu
```
Also adding similar egress qdisc shim for UDP large packets to avoid fragmentation.

taylor: Canary shows immediate improvement: v6 DNS retries dropped from 38% -> 4% on canary host. No adverse side effects so far. Proceeding to roll to all edge nodes in az20.

netops: As rolling, found one overlay node (az20-overlay-07) still advertising 9000 on tunnel interface despite central config. Manually set mtu 1500 and restarted overlay agent there.

jenny: Rolling the MTU change completed across az20 at 1870007120. Observed aggregate v6 DNS success climb back to normal.

cust-success: Updated impacted customers: "We applied mitigations (MSS clamp and MTU normalization) and are seeing recovery. Root cause under investigation: vendor auto-jumbo enabled on az20 virtual fabric. We're working with vendor for permanent fix." :email:

rafael: Root cause summary: vendor auto-jumbo + overlay mismatch -> intermittent fragmentation -> ICMPv6 PTB suppressed by firewall path -> PMTUD blackhole for v6 flows.

jenny: Action items: netops: require change window approval for fabric auto-features; infra: add MTU drift monitoring alert for each AZ; devex: document MSS clamp runbook; ops: include IPv6 PMTUD checks in chaos tests. Assigning tickets now.

infra-bot: Created tasks INFRA-5012, NETOPS-220, DEVEX-310, CHAOS-78

eng-oncall-bot: Handoff complete — @rafael is primary. jenny will remain available for follow-up.

taylor: Temporary policy: prefer IPv4 for public resolver traffic for 72h while vendor validates patch. Will revert when verified.

netops: Vendor SR opened (SR-99234). Vendor acknowledged replicated behavior and provided engineering patch ETA 3 days.

cust-success: We'll send a summary + ETA to the customers tomorrow.

jenny: Incident timeline: started 1870005555, mitigations applied (canary) 1870006800, full roll 1870007120, partial recovery observed 1870007240. Keeping incident open until vendor patch validated.

rafael: Postmortem owners: netops (root cause and vendor fix), infra (monitoring + runbooks), devex (playbook). Will schedule postmortem meeting in 48h.

pagerduty-bot: Incident updated: status=mitigated, oncall_owner=rafael, incident_id=INC-18700055

cust-success: Following up — customers appreciate quick mitigation. One customer requested permanent IPv6-only validation tests; flagged to chaos team.

jenny: Thanks everyone. Good coordination. Closing channel when vendor patch confirmed and monitoring stable for 48h. :white_check_mark:
